bug_semantics: After authenticating to /lucee/admin/web.cfm, an administrator can create and edit a scheduled task whose URL is attacker-controlled, whose publish flag is true, and whose file value is an arbitrary path such as the deployed webroot plus a .cfm filename. services.schedule.edit.cfm passes those values to cfadmin action="schedule" without constraining the destination. ExecutionThread fetches the URL and, when publish is enabled, writes the response directly to the task Resource with IOUtil.write or IOUtil.copy. Requesting the newly written .cfm makes Lucee compile and execute attacker-supplied CFML as the Lucee service account. There is no destination-path restriction, payload integrity check, or control preventing a fetched response from becoming executable server-side code.
flaw_origin: The design predates the Lucee Git repository and is inherited from Railo. Lucee's root commit 4e9afd8e48a71d89e7f34678edb7370c5d4b0b6c is a 3,457-file initial import that already contains both the arbitrary scheduled-task output path in the administrator and the unconditional publish-to-Resource implementation. Tracing the renamed classes into getrailo/railo reaches two consecutive 2009 whole-tree imports: 4b0d10b00807652c5b5b329dacdf417e8acdee63 adds the administrator surface and 99e969e528c6f5a9f726a229879a5e16a3112bdb adds the Java engine. Those are 315-file/20,455-line and 2,414-file/1,335,091-line imports, not the smallest commits that originally designed the behavior. No earlier source provenance is present in the public Git history, so the true BIC cannot be named.
ai_marker: The true BIC commit object is unavailable, so a BIC-only AI judgment cannot be made. For boundary confirmation only, `git cat-file commit 4b0d10b00807652c5b5b329dacdf417e8acdee63` and `git cat-file commit 99e969e528c6f5a9f726a229879a5e16a3112bdb` show human author and committer Michael Offner <michael@getrailo.com>, 2009-06-23 timestamps, message `Initial version`, and no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer. These aggregate import objects are explicitly not treated as the BIC.
evidence: Advisory mechanism and scope: NVD CVE-2025-34074 and GHSA-xr55-cjp7-wp4r describe authenticated administrator RCE by fetching a remote .cfm through a scheduled job, writing it to the webroot, and executing it as the Lucee service account; VulnCheck lists Lucee 5.x, Lucee 6.x, and all versions with scheduled-task functionality. The advisory bundle has no patched-version range.

Concrete attack flow: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rapid7/metasploit-framework/master/modules/exploits/multi/http/lucee_scheduled_job.rb authenticates to /lucee/admin/web.cfm, creates action=services.schedule, edits it with publish=true and file=<webroot>/<random>.cfm, executes the job, then GETs the .cfm. This independently matches the advisory's stated data flow.

Current source sink: `git show HEAD:core/src/main/cfml/context/admin/services.schedule.edit.cfm` shows cfadmin action="schedule" receiving url=form.url, publish=formBool('publish'), and file=nullIfEmpty(form.file); the same file exposes the Save-to-file checkbox and unrestricted text input. `git show HEAD:core/src/main/java/lucee/runtime/schedule/ExecutionThread.java` shows the HTTP GET followed by `if (!hasError && file != null && task.isPublish())` and then `IOUtil.write(file, ...)` or `IOUtil.copy(rsp.getContentAsStream(), file, true)`.

Lucee origin check in /home/hanqing/agents/ai-slop/.ai-slop/state/repos/lucee_lucee: `git log --follow -- core/src/main/java/lucee/runtime/schedule/ExecutionThread.java` terminates at root commit 4e9afd8e48a71d89e7f34678edb7370c5d4b0b6c. `git log --all -S'task.isPublish()' -- core/src/main/java/lucee/runtime/schedule/ExecutionThread.java` and `git log --all -S'publish="#formBool' -- core/src/main/cfml/context/admin/services.schedule.edit.cfm` each return only that root. `git show --shortstat 4e9afd8e48a71d89e7f34678edb7370c5d4b0b6c` reports 3,457 files and 593,622 insertions, establishing that it is a source import rather than the smallest BIC.

Predecessor trace: clone https://github.com/getrailo/railo and run `git log --all -S'task.isPublish()' -- railo-java/railo-core/src/railo/runtime/schedule/ExecutionThread.java`; it returns earliest visible write commit 99e969e528c6f5a9f726a229879a5e16a3112bdb with parent 4b0d10b00807652c5b5b329dacdf417e8acdee63. `git log master -L 89,145:railo-java/railo-core/src/railo/runtime/schedule/ExecutionThread.java --no-patch` likewise reaches 99e969e528c6f5a9f726a229879a5e16a3112bdb. At that commit, the file already performs the unrestricted HTTP-response-to-Resource copy.

Direct boundary verification: `git diff-tree --name-status -r 4b0d10b00807652c5b5b329dacdf417e8acdee63 99e969e528c6f5a9f726a229879a5e16a3112bdb -- railo-java/railo-core/src/railo/runtime/schedule/ExecutionThread.java` reports A, and `git cat-file -e 4b0d10b00807652c5b5b329dacdf417e8acdee63:railo-java/railo-core/src/railo/runtime/schedule/ExecutionThread.java` fails because the path is absent. Separately, `git log --all --follow -- railo-cfml/railo-admin/admin/services.schedule.edit.cfm` reaches 4b0d10b00807652c5b5b329dacdf417e8acdee63; its parent is 6b20542b4eeeec39064a4d38ea9fb88fa1d3fafe, and `git cat-file -e 6b20542b4eeeec39064a4d38ea9fb88fa1d3fafe:railo-cfml/railo-admin/admin/services.schedule.edit.cfm` fails because that path is absent. This verifies the visible import boundaries, but not absence from the unavailable pre-import source history.

Import-size check: in getrailo/railo, `git show --shortstat 4b0d10b00807652c5b5b329dacdf417e8acdee63` reports 315 files changed and 20,455 insertions; `git show --shortstat 99e969e528c6f5a9f726a229879a5e16a3112bdb` reports 2,414 files changed and 1,335,091 insertions. Both have message `Initial version`. Consequently neither can satisfy the protocol's smallest-real-BIC rule, and no member-commit decomposition is reconstructable from public Git objects.

Version and no-fix boundary: `git tag --contains 4e9afd8e48a71d89e7f34678edb7370c5d4b0b6c | sort -V` begins at Lucee 5.0.0.75. `git show 5.0.0.75:core/src/main/java/lucee/runtime/schedule/ExecutionThread.java` contains the publish guard and IOUtil.write/IOUtil.copy sink. The latest release tag visible in the validated clone, 8.0.0.166 at 87b2a5c9f916d23f64089c7428560185c48dcee7, contains the same sink, as does clone HEAD 3d41aa14b72b92b7d8b2b54fffdd32f7ff87a38e dated 2026-08-24. `git log --all --grep='CVE-2025-34074' --grep='GHSA-xr55-cjp7-wp4r' --grep='34074' -i` returns no commit. The issue therefore remains unpatched in the inspected public history; there is no closing or direct advisory fix SHA.

Commit-object marker check: `git cat-file commit 4b0d10b00807652c5b5b329dacdf417e8acdee63` and `git cat-file commit 99e969e528c6f5a9f726a229879a5e16a3112bdb` contain only tree, parent, Michael Offner author/committer lines, and `Initial version`; neither object has trailers or a bot identity. The Lucee import cannot substitute for the unavailable original BIC under the audit protocol.
reasoning: The vulnerability is a composition of an authenticated administrator control plane that accepts an arbitrary scheduled-task destination and an engine path that fetches attacker-selected bytes and writes them there. Putting a .cfm under the served webroot converts the file-write capability into service-account code execution. The behavior is present in the first Lucee release lineage and remains present after advisory publication, so fix_sha and direct_fix_sha are null because the case is explicitly unpatched in the inspected history. BIC reconstruction cannot stop at Lucee's root import: -S and -L trace the lines into Railo, where the first visible UI and engine objects are themselves adjacent whole-tree imports with parents lacking those paths. That proves only an import boundary, not the smallest commit that originally created the insecure design. Because the protocol forbids treating an import/squash aggregate as a BIC and permits AI evidence only from the true BIC commit object, the appropriate result is BLOCKED rather than NOT_AI, even though the visible 2009 import objects have no AI signal.
remaining_gap: The missing prerequisite is the pre-2009 Railo source-control history, or a provenance map from the 2009 `Initial version` imports to their original member commits. Without that public history, the smallest true introducer, its immediate parent, and its BIC-only commit-object marker cannot be verified. This is a genuine public-history boundary, not an unperformed repository query. No fix gap remains: the vulnerable sink is still present through tag 8.0.0.166 and validated-clone HEAD, so the case is unpatched in the inspected history.
